claim: Bone defect repair requires coordinated and concerted activities from both osteogenic and angiogenic cells.
source: Bone defect repair is a well-orchestrated process that requires coordinated and concerted activities from both osteogenic and angiogenic cells (Hankenson et al., 2011; Ai-Aql et al., 2008; Grosso et al., 2017; Hu and Olsen, 2017; Schott et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: The interdependent role of osteogenesis and angiogenesis is well documented.
source: While the interdependent role of osteogenesis and angiogenesis is well documented, the cellular and molecular events that take place at the osteogenic and angiogenic interface of bone defect repair remain superficially understood.
evidence: The claim references established scientific consensus.

claim: The cellular and molecular events at the osteogenic and angiogenic interface of bone defect repair remain superficially understood.
source: While the interdependent role of osteogenesis and angiogenesis is well documented, the cellular and molecular events that take place at the osteogenic and angiogenic interface of bone defect repair remain superficially understood.
evidence: The claim identifies a knowledge gap in the field.

claim: A functional blood vessel network consists of arteries, veins, and a capillary interface that connect arterial and venous vessels for proper vascular perfusion.
source: A functional blood vessel network consists of arteries, veins, and a capillary interface that connect arterial and venous vessels for proper vascular perfusion.
evidence: The claim describes established anatomical knowledge about blood vessel networks.

claim: Following injury, blood vessels are severed, and angiogenesis commences in response to hypoxia.
source: Following injury, blood vessels are severed, and angiogenesis commences in response to a low state of oxygen, that is, hypoxia.
evidence: The claim describes a known biological response to injury.

claim: Localized hypoxia stimulates endothelial cells to undergo sprouting of tip cells, proliferation of stalk cells, and expansion of continuous lumen.
source: Localized hypoxia stimulates endothelial cells (ECs) to undergo a series of changes including sprouting of the tip cells, proliferation of the stalk cells, and expansion of the continuous lumen, ultimately forming a functional capillary network to restore nutrients and oxygen supply to the site of the defect.
evidence: The claim describes known mechanisms of angiogenesis.

claim: Skeletal vasculature is uniquely patterned to adapt to the need and functionality of bone tissues at different anatomic sites.
source: Skeletal vasculature has been shown to be uniquely patterned to adapt to the need and functionality of bone tissues at different anatomic sites (Watson and Adams, 2018; Sivaraj and Adams, 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Type H (CD31highEmcnhigh) and type E (CD31highEmcnlow) vessels are shown coupling to OSX+ osteoblasts at the long bone metaphysis and Gli1+ bone progenitor cells at the cranial bone.
source: Type H (CD31highEmcnhigh) and type E (CD31highEmcnlow) vessels, as opposed to type L (CD31lowEmcnhigh) vessels, are shown coupling to OSX+ osteoblasts at the long bone metaphysis and Gli1+ bone progenitor cells at the cranial bone (Kusumbe et al., 2014; Ramasamy et al., 2014; Rindone et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Type E and type H vessels are derived from AplnCreER+ vessels that directly connect to arterioles and exhibit high flow rate.
source: Both type E and type H vessels are derived from AplnCreER+ vessels that directly connect to arterioles, exhibiting high flow rate and are further regulated by molecular pathways that control EC specification during development, that is, hypoxia inducible factor, BMP, and Notch pathways (Sivaraj and Adams, 2016; Langen et al., 2017; Xu et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Type E and type H vessels are regulated by hypoxia inducible factor, BMP, and Notch pathways.
source: Both type E and type H vessels are derived from AplnCreER+ vessels that directly connect to arterioles, exhibiting high flow rate and are further regulated by molecular pathways that control EC specification during development, that is, hypoxia inducible factor, BMP, and Notch pathways (Sivaraj and Adams, 2016; Langen et al., 2017; Xu et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Multiphoton laser scanning microscopy (MPLSM) enables high-resolution analyses of cranial bone tissue vascularization.
source: We have previously demonstrated an imaging platform for high-resolution analyses of cranial bone tissue vascularization via multiphoton laser scanning microscopy (MPLSM) (Zhai et al., 2021; Huang et al., 2015; Schilling et al., 2019; Zhang, 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research by the authors.

claim: MPLSM fluorescence excitation is intrinsically confined to a very small focal volume, permitting detection of scattered fluorescence light.
source: Compared with confocal microscopy which utilizes a pinhole to eliminate out-of-focus fluorescence, MPLSM fluorescence excitation is intrinsically confined to a very small focal volume, permitting detection of a great deal of scattered fluorescence light.
evidence: The claim describes a known technical property of MPLSM.

claim: Multiphoton excitation utilizes a longer wavelength laser to excite fluorescent molecules, allowing deeper penetration into tissues.
source: Since multiphoton excitation utilizes a longer wavelength laser to excite fluorescent molecules, penetration of the laser beam into the tissues is also considerably deeper, with further benefits of reduced photobleaching and photodamage (Hoover and Squier, 2013; Niesner and Hauser, 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: MPLSM can be used for imaging collagen matrix and bone tissue through second harmonic generation (SHG).
source: In addition to imaging fluorescence excitation, MPLSM can also be used for imaging collagen matrix and bone tissue through second harmonic generation (SHG), making it a powerful imaging platform for visualization and analysis of vascularization in bone tissue (Pendleton et al., 2020; Vielreicher et al., 2017; Chaudhary et al., 2016; Ranjit et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Two-photon phosphorescence lifetime microscopy (2P-PLIM) enables high spatial resolution measurements of partial oxygen tension (pO2) in living tissue.
source: Combining phosphorescence quenching with two-photon laser scanning microscopy, an optical technique known as two-photon phosphorescence lifetime microscopy (2P-PLIM) has been established. Equipped with two photon excitable oxygen probes, namely platinum porphyrin coumarin-343 (PtP-C343), this technique enables high spatial resolution measurements of partial oxygen tension (pO2) in living tissue (Finikova et al., 2008b; Lecoq et al., 2011; Sakadzić et al., 2010; Spencer et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Two-photon fluorescence lifetime imaging (2P-FLIM) can differentiate different metabolic states of cells and tissues by measuring free and bound NAD(P)H.
source: Another non-invasive technique developed to obtain information on cell metabolism and to differentiate different metabolic states of cells and tissues is the fluorescence lifetime-dependent measurements of free and bound NAD(P)H via two-photon microscopy (2P-FLIM) (Chance, 2004; Mayevsky and Chance, 2007; Winkler and Hirrlinger, 2015; Ma et al., 2016; Stringari et al., 2011; Stringari et al., 2012b; Stringari et al., 2015; Wright et al., 2012).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The intrinsic autofluorescence lifetimes of free and bound NAD(P)H reflect the metabolic state of single cells within the native microenvironment of living tissue.
source: This method exploits the intrinsic autofluorescence lifetimes of free and bound NAD(P)H, which reflect the metabolic state of single cells within the native microenvironment of the living tissue (Stringari et al., 2011; Stringari et al., 2012b; Stringari et al., 2015; Stringari et al., 2012a; Yaseen et al., 2009; Kolenc and Quinn, 2019; Datta et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: CD31 and EMCN define two distinct types of vessels at the site of cranial defect: CD31+EMCN+ and CD31+EMCN−.
source: As shown (Figures 1 and 2), CD31 and EMCN marked two distinct types of vessels at the site of cranial defect: CD31+EMCN+ (merging red and green channel to show as yellowish green or yellow) and CD31+EMCN− (red only with absence of EMCN staining).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: A relatively stronger staining of CD31 and EMCN in double positive vessels was observed at the site of active bone repair compared to regions of un-injured bone.
source: A relatively stronger staining of CD31 and EMCN in double positive vessels was observed at the site of active bone repair as compared to the regions of un-injured bone.
evidence: The claim is based on observations from the imaging data.

claim: Vessel organization and response at the superior and dura side of cranial bone are distinct.
source: As shown, vessel organization and response at the superior and dura side of cranial bone were distinct.
evidence: The claim is based on observations from the imaging data.

claim: Few vessels were found between days 1 and 5 on the surface of bone following injury from the superior side.
source: From the superior side, where the top 100–150 μm of the repair tissue was examined over a time course of 21 days (Figure 1, panels A, B, C, D, and E), we found few vessels between days 1 and 5 on the surface of bone following injury.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1.

claim: A large number of CD31+EMCN+ vessels sprouted out of the defect at day 5.
source: A large number of CD31+EMCN+ vessels sprouted out of the defect at day 5.
evidence: The claim is based on observations from the imaging data.

claim: The majority of the vessel networks at the superior side of cranial bone originated from dura side periosteum.
source: The vessels were further spread out and formed a connected network over the superior surface of bone, suggesting that the majority of the vessel networks at the superior side of cranial bone were originated from dura side periosteum.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observed pattern of vessel formation.

claim: CD31+EMCN− vessels followed a similar trend to CD31+EMCN+ vessels with significantly more vessels shown at days 14 and 21 around newly formed bone at the leading edge of the bone defect.
source: Compared to CD31+EMCN+ vessels (Figure 1, panel E1–7), CD31+EMCN− vessels (Figure 1, panel D1–7) followed a similar trend with significantly more vessels shown at days 14 and 21 around newly formed bone at the leading edge of the bone defect.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Col1a1-GFP+ osteoblasts appeared at the leading edge of the bone defect and along the channels of existing bone at day 10.
source: Col1a1-GFP+ osteoblasts (pseudocolored as cyan) appeared at the leading edge of the bone defect (Figure 1, panel C1–7) and some along the channels of the existing bone at day 10 (Figure 1F1, G1), in accordance with the appearance of some large diameter CD31+EMCN+ vessels in bone tissue.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Many CD31+EMCN+ vessels were observed to be lined by Col1a1-GFP+ osteoblasts and intertwined with CD31+EMCN− vessels at days 10, 14, and 21 in newly formed bone undergoing active remodeling.
source: Many of these CD31+EMCN+ vessels were observed to be lined by Col1a1-GFP+ osteoblasts and intertwined with CD31+EMCN− vessels at days 10, 14, and 21 in newly formed bone undergoing active remodeling (Figure 1, panels F and G, arrows).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Sporadic osteoblast colonies were found at the dura side periosteum in non-injured bone.
source: As shown, sporadic osteoblast colonies were found at the dura side periosteum in non-injured bone (Figure 2D1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Major CD31+EMCN+ and CD31+EMCN− vessels can be readily identified at the dura periosteum, suggesting that dura periosteum was better vascularized.
source: Distinct from the superior periosteum where fewer large vessels were found on the surface, major CD31+EMCN+ and CD31+EMCN− vessels can be readily identified at the dura periosteum via CD31 and EMCN immunofluorescence staining, suggesting that dura periosteum was better vascularized (Figure 2, panel A1-F1).
evidence: The claim is based on observations from the imaging data and inference.

claim: Healing was initiated following injury at day 1 with visibly larger osteoblast colonies seen around the injury site.
source: Healing was initiated following injury at day 1 with visibly larger osteoblast colonies seen around the injury site (Figure 2, panels A2–F2).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The expansion of Col1a1-GFP+ cells peaked at days 5 and 10 post injury, followed by progressively enhanced SHG indicating progressive bone formation on bone surface.
source: The expansion of Col1a1-GFP+ cells (Figure 2B 1-7 and Figure 2D 1-7, pseudocolored as cyan) peaked at days 5 and 10 post injury, followed by progressively enhanced SHG (Figure 2A 1-7, gray to white), indicating progressive bone formation on bone surface.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2.

claim: CD31+EMCN+ vessels initiated rapid sprouting and expansion as early as day 3 within the defect and in regions closely associated with Col1a1-GFP+ cells.
source: Examination of the spatiotemporal changes of the two types of vessels showed that CD31+EMCN+ vessels (Figure 2, panel C1–7 indicated as yellow, and panel F1–7 indicated as green) initiated rapid sprouting and expansion as early as day 3 within the defect and in the regions closely associated with Col1a1-GFP+ cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The majority of CD31+EMCN+ vessels showed strong staining of both CD31 and EMCN.
source: The majority of these vessels showed strong staining of both CD31 and EMCN.
evidence: The claim is based on observations from the imaging data.

claim: The expansion of CD31+EMCN+ vessels was supported by significantly increased diameter of the main venule at the peak of angiogenesis.
source: The expansion of these CD31+EMCN+ vessels was supported by significantly increased diameter of the main venule at the peak of angiogenesis.
evidence: The claim is based on observations from the imaging data.

claim: The rapid expansion of CD31+EMCN+ vessels was transient and quickly reverted back to normal density as the expansion of Col1a1-GFP cells subsided.
source: Interestingly, the rapid expansion of CD31+EMCN+ vessels was transient and quickly reverted back to normal density as the expansion of Col1a1-GFP cells subsided.
evidence: The claim is based on observations from the imaging data.

claim: Branching and extension of CD31+EMCN− vessels were significantly delayed and only observed at day 10 when new bone tissue started building up and underwent remodeling.
source: Compared with CD31+EMCN+ vessels, branching and extension of CD31+EMCN− vessels (Figure 2, panel C1–7 shown as red, and panel E1–7 as red) were significantly delayed and the induction only observed at day 10 when new bone tissue started building up and further underwent remodeling.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2.

claim: The expansion of CD31+EMCN+ vessels peaked at day 5, coinciding with the expansion of GFP+ cells.
source: Consistently, the expansion of CD31+EMCN+ vessels peaked at day 5, coinciding with the expansion of GFP+ cells.
evidence: The claim is based on quantitative analyses shown in Figure 2G-L.

claim: The extension and branching of CD31+EMCN− vessels coincided with enhanced SHG, indicating that increased CD31+EMCN− vessels were associated with bone tissue deposition and remodeling.
source: In comparison, the extension and branching of CD31+EMCN− vessels coincided with enhanced SHG, indicating that increased CD31+EMCN− vessels were associated with bone tissue deposition and remodeling.
evidence: The claim is based on quantitative analyses shown in Figure 2G-L.

claim: AplnCreER-labeled vessels were completely overlapping with CD31+EMCN+ vessels and excluded from CD31+EMCN− vessels within the defect and in bone channels.
source: As shown (Figure 3, panel A1–8), AplnCreER-labeled vessels were completely overlapping with CD31+EMCN+ vessels, and excluded from CD31+EMCN− vessels within the defect (Figure 3A5) and in bone channels (Figure 3A8).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3.

claim: BmxCreER; Ai14 reporter mice labeled nearly exclusively arterioles and capillary vessels descending from arterioles in the healing bone tissue.
source: In contrast, in a similar experiment, BmxCreER; Ai14 reporter mice labeled nearly exclusively arterioles and capillary vessels descending from arterioles in the healing bone tissue (Figure 3, panel B1–4).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3.

claim: BmxCreER-labeled vessels were mutually exclusive from EMCN+ vessels at the defect or in bone.
source: These vessels, shown as red, were mutually exclusive from EMCN+ vessels (shown as green) at the defect (Figure 3B1–3) or in bone (Figure 3B4).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3.

claim: CD31+EMCN+ vessels were derived from AplnCreER+ sprouting ECs whereas CD31+EMCN− vessels extended from BmxCreER+ arterial ECs.
source: These experiments demonstrated that CD31+EMCN+ vessels were derived from AplnCreER+ sprouting ECs whereas CD31+EMCN− vessels extended from BmxCreER+ arterial ECs.
evidence: The claim is based on the experimental results shown in Figure 3.

claim: Significantly lower pO2 levels were found at days 10, 17, and 31 post surgery in vessels and interstitium less than 150 μm from clusters of osteoblasts.
source: As shown, significantly lower pO2 levels were found at days 10, 17, and 31 post surgery in vessels and interstitium less than 150 μm from clusters of osteoblasts (Figure 4H1 and K, p<0.05).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4.

claim: pO2 measurements were recorded at the lowest levels at day 17 (mean = 23.69 ± 10.39 mmHg), indicating a hypoxic environment.
source: Of note is that pO2 measurements were recorded at the lowest levels at day 17 (mean = 23.69 ± 10.39 mmHg) (p<0.05), indicating a hypoxic environent, presumably due to an increased metabolic need associated with the expansion of osteoblasts in the newly forming bone.
evidence: The claim is supported by data and includes an inference about the cause.

claim: The pO2 in all areas gradually increased as more vessel network formed and became mature over the 31-day period.
source: Interestingly, the pO2 in all areas gradually increased as more vessel network formed and became mature over the 31-day period.
evidence: The claim is based on observations from the imaging data.

claim: Intra-vascular pO2 measurements made within the defect at day 10 were significantly higher (mean = 49.66 ± 17.97 mmHg) than those in the defect interstitium (mean = 35.81 ± 10.8 mmHg).
source: Intra-vascular pO2 measurements made within the defect at day 10 were significantly higher (mean = 49.66 ± 17.97 mmHg) than those in the defect interstitium (mean = 35.81 ± 10.8 mmHg, Figure 5B, p<0.05).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The BmxCreER+ vessels had higher pO2 than the nearby interstitial space at days 10, 17, and 31 post-surgery.
source: The BmxCreER+ vessels had higher pO2 than the nearby interstitial space at days 10, 17, and 31 post-surgery (Figure 5B, *, p<0.05).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Measurements of pO2 significantly increased within all regions with the highest levels recorded from the vessels in the defect at ~74.68 ± 7.64 mmHg at day 31.
source: Measurements of pO2 significantly increased within all regions with the highest levels recorded from the vessels in the defect at ~74.68 ± 7.64 mmHg at day 31.
evidence: The claim is based on observations from the imaging data.

claim: A significant correlation was found between pO2 and distance from the edge of the bone defect at days 24 and 31.
source: However, a significant correlation was found at days 24 and 31, indicating that at the later stages of healing, there was a slightly lower environmental pO2 along the area of newly formed bone, potenitally due to increased oxygen usage at the area (Figures 5C3 and 4, day 24: R=0.171, p=0.042; day 31: R=0.253, p=0.006).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The mean pO2 in BmxCreER+ vessels was significantly higher than those of AplnCreER+ vessels when measured at comparable time points and locations.
source: It is worth noting that the mean pO2 in BmxCreER+ vessels was significantly higher than those of AplnCreER+ vessels when measured at comparable time points and locations, with the measurements at days 24 and 31 showing much larger differences (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: AplnCreER+ ECs had a significantly lower NAD(P)H τM than osteoblasts, suggesting that compared to osteoblasts AplnCreER+ ECs prefer glycolysis over OxPhos.
source: Longitudinal measurement of NAD(P)H τM suggested that AplnCreER+ ECs had a significantly lower NAD(P)H τM than osteoblasts (Figure 6C, P<0.001), suggesting that compared to osteoblasts AplnCreER+ ECs prefer glycolysis over OxPhos.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 6 and includes an inference about metabolic preference.

claim: AplnCreER+ ECs were less sensitive to the changes of environmental pO2 compared to osteoblasts which shifted the τM to a lower value at day 17 when pO2 was lower.
source: Furthermore, when compared to osteoblasts which shifted the τM to a lower value at day 17 when pO2 was lower (p<0.001), AplnCreER+ ECs were less sensitive to the changes of environmental pO2 at the same locations (Figure 6B, C).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 6.

claim: Osteoblasts in osteogenic media had an increasing τM longitudinally from 1.55±0.13 ns at day 17 to 1.75±0.18 ns at day 24.
source: Measurement of NAD(P)H τM showed that osteoblasts in osteogenic media had an increasing τM longitudinally from 1.55±0.13 ns at day 17 to 1.75±0.18 ns at day 24, whereas cells in regular media had a consistently similar τM of ~1.3 ns among all time points.
evidence: The claim is supported by data from in vitro experiments.

claim: AplnCreER+ ECs had a lower NAD(P)H τM than GFP+ osteoblasts and GFP− stromal cells at all time points examined in vitro.
source: In comparison, AplnCreER+ ECs had a lower NAD(P)H τM than GFP+ osteoblasts and GFP− stromal cells at all time points examined (Figure 6E, p>0.05).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 6.

claim: The NAD(P)H τM from AplnCreER+ ECs was similar in osteogenic and regular media.
source: Additionally, the NAD(P)H τM from AplnCreER+ ECs was similar in osteogenic and regular media (Figure 6E, p>0.05), supporting our finding in vivo which suggests that compared with ECs, osteoblasts used more OxPhos at the site of healing.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 6 and includes an inference.

claim: CD31 and EMCN mark arterial and venous capillary network with CD31+EMCN+ vessels derived from AplnCreER+ sprouting ECs and CD31+EMCN− vessels from BmxCreER+ arterial ECs.
source: Our data show that CD31 and EMCN mark arterial and venous capillary network with CD31+EMCN+ vessels derived from AplnCreER+ sprouting ECs and CD31+EMCN− vessels from BmxCreER+ arterial ECs.
evidence: The claim summarizes findings from the study.

claim: The two types of vessels demonstrate distinct dynamics in response to injury with osteoblast clusters tightly coupled to CD31+EMCN+ (AplnCreER+) vessels at the regenerative interface.
source: The two types of vessels demonstrate distinct dynamics in response to injury with osteoblast clusters tightly coupled to CD31+EMCN+ (AplnCreER+) vessels at the regenerative interface.
evidence: The claim summarizes findings from the study.

claim: AplnCreER+ ECs utilize more glycolysis than Col1a1-GFP+ osteoblasts at the site of repair.
source: By probing local pO2 via 2P-PLIM and cellular metabolism via 2P-FLIM, we further show that AplnCreER+ ECs utilize more glycolysis than Col1a1-GFP+ osteoblasts at the site of repair.
evidence: The claim summarizes findings from the study.

claim: Energy metabolism of osteoblasts is more sensitive to pO2 changes than that of AplnCreER+ ECs.
source: Energy metabolism of osteoblasts is also more sensitive to pO2 changes than that of AplnCreER+ ECs.
evidence: The claim summarizes findings from the study.

claim: CD31+EMCN− vessels exhibit higher mean pO2 than CD31+EMCN+ vessels at the osteogenic and angiogenic interface during nanofiber-mediated cranial defect repair.
source: Utilizing an intravital MPLSM imaging approach, we have previously shown that CD31+EMCN− vessels exhibit higher mean pO2 than CD31+EMCN+ vessels at the osteogenic and angiogenic interface during nanofiber-mediated cranial defect repair (Zhai et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior research by the authors.

claim: CD31+EMCN+ vessels expand rapidly, coinciding with the expansion of the clusters of Col1a1-GFP+ osteoblasts.
source: Our data demonstrate distinct dynamics of the two types of vessels marked by CD31 and EMCN in response to injury: CD31+EMCN+ vessels expand rapidly, coinciding with the expansion of the clusters of Col1a1-GFP+ osteoblasts, while CD31+EMCN− vessels show a delayed response to injury, with enhanced branching and extension of the vessels observed at a late stage of healing, when formation of vascular channels within bone tissue is evident.
evidence: The claim summarizes findings from the study.

claim: CD31+EMCN− vessels show a delayed response to injury, with enhanced branching and extension observed at a late stage of healing when formation of vascular channels within bone tissue is evident.
source: Our data demonstrate distinct dynamics of the two types of vessels marked by CD31 and EMCN in response to injury: CD31+EMCN+ vessels expand rapidly, coinciding with the expansion of the clusters of Col1a1-GFP+ osteoblasts, while CD31+EMCN− vessels show a delayed response to injury, with enhanced branching and extension of the vessels observed at a late stage of healing, when formation of vascular channels within bone tissue is evident.
evidence: The claim summarizes findings from the study.

claim: The differential dynamics of the angiogenic response reflects the intrinsic differences between venous and arterial ECs in response to bone injury.
source: The differential dynamics of the angiogenic response reflects the intrinsic differences between venous and arterial ECs in response to bone injury, which could be attributed to the fundamental differences in the biology of the two types of vessels (dela Paz and D'Amore, 2009; Hwa et al., 2017; Aitsebaomo et al., 2008; Simons and Eichmann, 2015; Herbert and Stainier, 2011).
evidence: The claim is an inference supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The differential dynamics of angiogenesis from the two types of vessels could be attributed to the repertoire of angiogenic factors produced by osteoblasts to induce a blood vessel network specialized for bone regeneration and homeostasis.
source: The differential dynamics of angiogenesis from the two types of vessels could also be attributed to the repertoire of angiogenic factors produced by osteoblasts to induce a blood vessel network that is specialized for bone regeneration and homeostasis (Schipani et al., 2009; Stegen and Carmeliet, 2018; Stegen et al., 2015; Gerstenfeld et al., 2003).
evidence: The claim is speculation supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The rapid expansion of the CD31+EMCN+ vessels is transient and quickly subsides when osteoblasts become more mature and when significant bone matrix deposition and remodeling follow.
source: It is worth noting that the rapid expansion of the CD31+EMCN+ vessels is transient and quickly subsides when osteoblasts become more mature and when significant bone matrix deposition and remodeling follow.
evidence: The claim is based on observations from the imaging data.

claim: The regression of the vessels is necessary for organization of a specialized bone vasculature, specifically the formation of type H vessels in new bone tissue.
source: The regression of the vessels is necessary for organization of a specialized bone vasculature, specifically the formation of type H vessels in new bone tissue.
evidence: The claim is an inference based on the observed data.

claim: The formation of a specialized vascular network in bone involves concerted activities from osteoblasts, osteoclasts as well as subsets of ECs.
source: This finding is also consistent with more recent studies which link specialized osteoclastic activities with organization and formation of type H vessel formation in bone (Romeo et al., 2019; Kohara et al., 2022; Liu et al., 2021), suggesting that the formation of a specialized vascular network in bone involves concerted activities from osteoblasts, osteoclasts as well as subsets of ECs.
evidence: The claim is an inference supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Revascularization at the superior side of cranial bone is largely dependent upon the rapid expansion of the vasculature from the dura periosteum.
source: By analyzing the time-dependent changes of bone and vessel formation at the superior and dura periosteum of cranial defect repair, we further show that revascularization at the superior side of cranial bone is largely dependent upon the rapid expansion of the vasculature from the dura periosteum.
evidence: The claim is based on observations from the imaging data.

claim: Progenitor cells located at the dura periosteum and in the marrow space are the major sources of bone forming cells during healing.
source: Similarly, progenitor cells located at the dura periosteum and in the marrow space are the major sources of bone forming cells during healing, as these cells are the first to respond to injury (Figures 1 and 2).
evidence: The claim is based on observations from the imaging data.

claim: The differences in the response to injury at the two different sites of periosteum could be attributed to the extent of damage inflicted on vessels and progenitor cells during initial surgery.
source: The differences in the response to injury at the two different sites of periosteum could be attributed to the extent of damage inflicted on vessels and progenitor cells during initial surgery, in which the dura periosteal cells/vessels are better preserved.
evidence: The claim is speculation about the cause of observed differences.

claim: The difference in response to injury at the two periosteum sites could be due to the different density and distribution of vessel types present on the superior and dura periosteum.
source: However, the difference could also be due to the different density and distribution of vessel types present on the superior and dura periosteum.
evidence: The claim is speculation about the cause of observed differences.

claim: Apelin is a highly conserved secreted peptide that binds and acts as an endogenous ligand for a G protein-coupled receptor APJ.
source: Apelin, encoded by gene Apln, is a highly conserved secreted peptide that binds and acts as an endogenous ligand for a G protein-coupled receptor APJ (del Toro et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Apln is expressed in endothelial tip cells and sprouting ECs in various organs.
source: Apln is expressed in endothelial tip cells and sprouting ECs in various organs (Langen et al., 2017; Liu et al., 2015; Chen et al., 2016; Kocijan et al., 2021) and has been shown to be significantly increased in response to a hypoxic environment (Ronkainen et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Apln has been shown to be significantly increased in response to a hypoxic environment.
source: Apln is expressed in endothelial tip cells and sprouting ECs in various organs (Langen et al., 2017; Liu et al., 2015; Chen et al., 2016; Kocijan et al., 2021) and has been shown to be significantly increased in response to a hypoxic environment (Ronkainen et al., 2007).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Nearly all CD31+EMCN+ capillary vessels are labeled by AplnCreER including vessels tightly associated with osteoblasts following injury at day 14, excluding CD31+EMCN− vessels derived from arterial vessels.
source: By tracing AplnCreER+ vessels during repair, our current study shows that nearly all CD31+EMCN+ capillary vessels are labeled by AplnCreER including vessels tightly associated with osteoblasts following injury at day 14, excluding CD31+EMCN− vessels derived from arterial vessels (Figure 3A 1-8).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3.

claim: AplnCreER-derived vessels give rise to CD31highEMCNhigh type H and E vessels that are tightly coupled to osteoblasts during bone development.
source: This result is consistent with the previous study which shows that AplnCreER-derived vessels give rise to CD31highEMCNhigh type H and E vessels that are tightly coupled to osteoblasts during bone development (Langen et al., 2017), suggesting that AplnCreER is a useful tool to study vessel coupling with osteoblasts.
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: AplnCreER+ EC robustly labels venules and venous capillaries but not arterial ECs at the site of injury.

claim: Endothelial bone marrow tyrosine kinase Bmx is a gene known to be expressed in ECs of arterial vessels.
source: In contrast to Apln, endothelial bone marrow tyrosine kinase Bmx is a gene known to be expressed in ECs of arterial vessels (Rajantie et al., 2001; Ekman et al., 1997).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The BmxCreER mouse model has been shown to largely label arterial vessels during retinal angiogenesis.
source: The BmxCreER mouse model has been shown to largely label arterial vessels during retinal angiogenesis (Ehling et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: BmxCreER+ vessels are primarily arterial CD31+EMCN− vessels directly extended from arterioles at the healing site.
source: Consistent with this, our current study shows that BmxCreER+ vessels are primarily arterial CD31+EMCN− vessels directly extended from arterioles at the healing site (Figures 3B1–4).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3.

claim: BmxCreER+ vessels show higher mean pO2 than AplnCreER+ vessels at a similar location, particularly when the vessel network at the defect site becomes more mature and stable at a later stage.
source: BmxCreER+ vessels show higher mean pO2 than AplnCreER+ vessels at a similar location, particularly when the vessel network at the defect site becomes more mature and stable at a later stage (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: BmxCreER+ vessels exhibit a slow response to injury during the course of healing, consistent with what is observed in CD31+EMCN− vessels.
source: In contrast to AplnCreER+ vessels which are abundant and subject to dynamic changes at the site of the defect, BmxCreER+ vessels exhibit a slow response to injury during the course of healing, consistent with what is observed in CD31+EMCN− vessels.
evidence: The claim is based on observations from the imaging data.

claim: AplnCreER+ vessels closer to osteoblast clusters have significantly lower pO2 at days 10 and 17, coinciding with osteoblast expansion.
source: Despite heterogeneous pO2 distribution within blood vessels, our analyses show that AplnCreER+ vessels closer to osteoblast clusters have significantly lower pO2 at days 10 and 17 (Figure 4H, I), coinciding with osteoblast expansion, indicating enhanced demand for oxygen supply and potentially enhanced consumption of oxygen at the osteogenic and angiogenic interface during early stages of healing.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4 and includes an inference.

claim: BmxCreER+ vessels at days 10 and 17 do not show changes of pO2 as a function of distance.
source: In contrast to AplnCreER+ vessels which are often found to be close to osteoblasts, BmxCreER+ vessels at days 10 and 17 do not show changes of pO2 as a function of distance (Figures 5C1–2), suggesting that perhaps the dip of pO2 is vessel type dependent and could be attributed to the close coupling of AplnCreER+ vessels with osteoblast clusters at the leading edge of the defect.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 5 and includes speculation.

claim: Glycolysis is the primary energy producing mechanism in ECs.
source: Our data show that AplnCreER+ ECs prefer glycolysis and are less sensitive to microenvironmental pO2 changes at the site of defect repair, consistent with reports that show that glycolysis is the primary energy producing mechanisms in ECs (Eelen et al., 2018), and glycolysis is highly favored during sprouting (De Bock et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: Glycolysis is highly favored during sprouting.
source: Our data show that AplnCreER+ ECs prefer glycolysis and are less sensitive to microenvironmental pO2 changes at the site of defect repair, consistent with reports that show that glycolysis is the primary energy producing mechanisms in ECs (Eelen et al., 2018), and glycolysis is highly favored during sprouting (De Bock et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citation to prior research.

claim: By choosing glycolysis for ATP production, ECs allow oxygen diffusion to neighboring cells to support healing.
source: By choosing glycolysis for ATP production, ECs allow oxygen diffusion to neighboring cells to support healing.
evidence: The claim is an inference about the functional consequence of EC metabolism.

claim: Low oxygen status is favored by osteoblastic aerobic glycolytic metabolism at the site of bone repair and regeneration.
source: This is consistent with the data that show low oxygen status is favored by osteoblastic aerobic glycolytic metabolism at the site of bone repair and regeneration (Lee et al., 2017).

source: The heterogeneous pO2 could not be attributed to the heterogeneous vessel diameter distribution at the site of repair since our data showed poor correlation of pO2 value with the vessel diameter at the site of repair (data not shown).
evidence: The claim is based on data analysis (though data not shown).

claim: The pO2 heterogeneity has critical functional consequences for different cell types in bone and could be important for constitution of various stem cell niches.
source: The pO2 heterogeneity has critical functional consequences for different cell types in bone and could be important for constitution of various stem cell niches (Itkin et al., 2016; Chen et al., 2020; Sivan et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is speculation supported by citations to prior research.

source: It is also worth noting that while the range of pO2 in CD31+EMCN+ vessels falls within the reported blood pO2 in venous vessels, the mean pO2 in CD31+EMCN− capillary vessels is lower than reported in arterial blood (Marenzana and Arnett, 2013), likely due to the active exchange and consumption of oxygen at the repair site.
evidence: The claim is based on comparison with literature and includes an inference.

evidence: The claim is supported by citations to prior research.
